name: Monotone endpoint enclosure over a declared finite box on Q, its per-tick iterated form, and the nested-box condition, with fail-closed bounds -- NEW DERIVATION / PROPOSAL -- not yet in Toledo

statement.latest: \text{Let } B=\prod_{i<n}[lo_i,hi_i]\subset\mathbb{Q}^n \text{ be a declared finite box and } \sigma_i\in\{+,-\} \text{ a declared sign pattern; } f:\mathbb{Q}^n\to\mathbb{Q} \text{ non-decreasing in every } i\in I^+ \text{ and non-increasing in every } i\in I^-. \text{ With } x^{lo*}_i := lo_i \,(i\in I^+),\ hi_i\,(i\in I^-) \text{ and } x^{hi*} \text{ the reverse: } \boxed{\forall x\in B:\ f(x^{lo*})\le f(x)\le f(x^{hi*})} \text{ (both corners lie in } B\text{, so both endpoints are attained). Iterated: if } D_{t+1}=g(D_t,u_t),\ g \text{ non-decreasing in } D \text{ and } \sigma\text{-monotone in } u,\ u_t\in B_t,\ D^{lo}_0\le D_0\le D^{hi}_0, \text{ then } \boxed{D^{lo}_t\le D_t\le D^{hi}_t\ \forall t\in\mathbb{N}} \text{ with } D^{lo},D^{hi} \text{ run at the lower/upper corners. Nested box: } B_c\sqsubseteq B_p :\Leftrightarrow lo^p_i\le lo^c_i\le hi^c_i\le hi^p_i\ \forall i \Rightarrow [f(x^{lo*}_c),f(x^{hi*}_c)]\subseteq[f(x^{lo*}_p),f(x^{hi*}_p)]. \text{ Three-state interval readout } cl(lo,hi;\theta):=\mathrm{classify}\big(\tfrac{hi-lo}{2},\tfrac{lo+hi}{2}-\theta\big) \text{ (D/M.71--76, exact renaming): } Sp\iff\theta<lo,\ Sm\iff hi<\theta,\ Sz\iff lo=hi=\theta,\ Sbot\iff lo\le\theta\le hi,\ lo\ne hi; \text{ for nested intervals a determinate parent state is inherited and never flipped. } \boxed{\text{REFUSED (BOUND\_MISSING | BOUND\_ORDER | NOT\_NESTED)}} \text{ for the layer that lacks a declared endpoint, has } lo>hi, \text{ or is compared to a non-nested layer -- never } \pm\infty.
statement.note_ascii: NEW DERIVATION / PROPOSAL -- not yet in Toledo. Domain-generic (nothing here mentions water). For a declared finite box B on Q^n and a declared sign pattern, a coordinate-wise monotone f is enclosed by its values at the two declared corners (lo* = lower on increasing coordinates, upper on decreasing ones; hi* = reverse), both corners are points of B (tight), a per-tick recursion that is non-decreasing in its state stays enclosed at every tick by the two corner runs, and a child box nested in a parent box has its enclosure nested in the parent's. The interval three-state readout is D/M.71-76 classify with floor := (hi-lo)/2 and v := (lo+hi)/2 - theta (renaming, not a new classifier): ROBUST (Sp) iff theta < lo, BELOW (Sm) iff hi < theta, AT_THRESHOLD (Sz) iff lo = hi = theta, POSSIBLE (Sbot) iff lo <= theta <= hi with lo <> hi; boundary convention: lo = theta < hi is POSSIBLE (conservative). For nested intervals a ROBUST/BELOW parent is inherited by every child and can never be flipped by it; without nesting it can (counterexample recorded). A missing endpoint REFUSES that layer only (BOUND_MISSING), lo > hi is BOUND_ORDER, a non-nested strict refinement is NOT_NESTED. Registered ONCE here; PROP-FLOOD-08 uses it directly for E_k (excess_sigma_monotone); the interval form of L is the same form, proved directly in 08 (load_ratio_enclosure), not a corollary; PROP-FLOOD-10 uses cl, refine_check and excess directly and the level-1 box step wb_step_enclosure. No second enclosure object is registered. v1.1: a BOX-RESTRICTED form is added (monotonicity required only between points of the declared box -- enclosure_sound_box), because products such as P*A*c are monotone only on the non-negative orthant; global monotonicity is its special case (sigma_monotone_box). Strict refinement rejects reversed endpoints of either layer (BOUND_ORDER) before the nesting test, and a passed check licenses the no-flip readout (checked_refinement_no_flip).

claim_boundary: A finite order-theoretic statement about declared boxes and monotone maps on Q. It asserts nothing about which maps a physical system obeys: each use must prove (or cite a proof of) the monotonicity of its own map, and the enclosure is only as good as the declared box. No probability, no distribution inside the box, no continuum limit, no infinite endpoint.
non_claims: Not a probabilistic interval: [f(lo*), f(hi*)] is a guaranteed range for inputs inside the declared box, not a confidence interval.
Not valid for non-monotone maps: a map that is not monotone in some coordinate needs a different enclosure (not supplied).
The screening recursion max(0, D + P - C) being monotone does not promote it to a readout; it stays a screening heuristic (PROP-FLOOD-08 non-claims).
D/M.77.v1 (bot_monotone_in_floor) is the same-centre special case; the nested-box theorem is the delta because a nested child moves both centre and half-width.

monotonicity: Proved (Th_coqc-in-proposal-lane, see coq_theorems): enclosure_sound, iterated_enclosure, nested_enclosure; instances excess_sigma_monotone, screen_step_mono_D, screen_step_sigma, wb_step_enclosure.
honest_caveats: Tier stays Dr/unverified until the normal Toledo review path; machine-checked lemmas in a proposal-lane file do not by themselves promote a proposal.

The sign pattern is a declaration; a wrong sign declaration makes the enclosure wrong without any Coq error, because the Coq theorem takes monotonicity as a hypothesis -- each instance must carry its own monotonicity proof (the three used downstream do).
The boundary convention lo = theta < hi => POSSIBLE is conservative for the strict (ROBUST) claim; the worst-first firing rule of PROP-FLOOD-10 uses hi >= theta, which includes equality.
falsifier: A declared box, a map with a proved sign pattern, and a point inside the box whose value falls outside [f(lo*), f(hi*)] would falsify the enclosure (the Coq proof rules this out for the stated hypotheses, so an observed violation locates a wrong declaration: box, sign pattern, or a non-monotone map used as if monotone). A nested child whose determinate state is opposite to its determinate parent with no input error falsifies the nesting declaration.
